html:
Paisius of Hilendar was a Bulgarian monk at the Hilendar monastery on Mount Athos, born in 1722 near Bansko, who in 1762 finished the Slavonic-Bulgarian History, the founding text of the Bulgarian national revival.

Angered that Greek and Serbian monks looked down on Bulgarians, he gathered sources and wrote a short history of the medieval Bulgarian tsars and saints. He urged Bulgarians to be proud of their past and their language and not to become Greeks. The book was copied by hand and read aloud for decades before it was printed in 1844. Bulgarians see it as the start of the revival that led to their own church, schools and the April Uprising. He is a saint of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church, and his work kept the memory of Simeon and the old kingdoms alive.
sum: Paisius of Hilendar was a Bulgarian monk at the Hilendar monastery on Mount Athos, born in 1722 near Bansko, who in 1762 finished the Slavonic-Bulgarian History, the founding text of the Bulgarian national revival.
